reading.body:
The Model Context Protocol's server reference repository alone has accumulated nearly 90,000 stars, making it one of the most-watched infrastructure repositories in the ecosystem, and the eight official repositories together total over 158,000 stars.

The star distribution reveals a clear hierarchy of developer interest. The servers repository draws roughly four times the attention of the Python SDK, which itself leads the TypeScript SDK by nearly two to one. The inspector, a visual testing tool, sits in the middle of the ranking with around 11,000 stars, ahead of the registry and the three language SDKs maintained in collaboration with Google, Microsoft, and Spring AI. That the registry, the directory that would let developers discover MCP servers, holds fewer than 8,000 stars suggests the cataloguing layer is less mature than the implementation layer.

All eight repositories remain active, with the most recent pushes recorded within days of the August 31 data snapshot. Five carry custom licences and two carry MIT licences, which matters for any organization assessing how freely these components can be incorporated into commercial infrastructure. The data covers only the official modelcontextprotocol organization repositories on GitHub and does not capture third-party SDKs, community forks, or the total number of servers listed in the registry itself, so it measures the protocol's official tooling surface, not the full scale of adoption.
